obligations.text: This procedure concerns one fictional U.S. bank, one opened investigation, one retained human reporting decision and one initial Suspicious Activity Report (SAR). The suspect was identified on the date of initial detection. Joint filings, continuing reports, criminal determinations, account closure, freezes and changes to customer funds are outside this first operation. A separately governed customer message may request an explanation of underlying transactions without revealing the SAR's existence.

For banks, the cited rule governs SAR filing, specifies the initial-detection clock, requires five-year retention from filing and restricts disclosure of SAR information. Its identified-suspect filing period is 30 calendar days. The possible additional period for identifying an unknown suspect does not apply to this selected case. Situations requiring immediate attention have an additional immediate law-enforcement notification duty. [31 CFR 1020.320(b), (d) and (e)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-31/subtitle-B/chapter-X/part-1020/subpart-C/section-1020.320)

The September 2, 2026 joint statement permits communication of underlying facts without revealing that a SAR exists. Other privacy and bank-policy restrictions remain applicable. [FinCEN and banking agencies' joint statement](https://www.fincen.gov/system/files/2026-09/Joint-Statement-on-SAR-Confidentiality.pdf)

The April 2026 filing instructions permit a limited CSV attachment, distinguish supporting records from transmitted content, describe complete corrected/amended reports and explain that the guidance's 90/120-day continuing-report schedule is optional. This case selects no filing attachment and no continuing report. [FinCEN SAR filing instructions, sections 6.1.3, 6.1.4 and 6.1.6](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/FinCENSARFilingInstructions.pdf)

All later clauses are selected fictional bank policy unless marked as a host premise or unresolved assumption. Human approval roles, separation rules, review thresholds, reminder times and gateway behavior are not asserted to be universal federal requirements.

The bank identity is MRB-US-01. Investigation MRB-CASE-074 concerns customer customer-074, account account-074 and three completed outgoing USD transfers dated September 8, 10 and 12, 2026, totaling USD 84,000.00. The fictional transaction records are MRB-TXN-081, MRB-TXN-082 and MRB-TXN-083, each revision 1. The reporting period is September 8 through September 12, 2026. The agent cannot treat these facts as a finding of criminal guilt.

Initial Detection Record MRB-DETECTION-074 revision 1 records September 14, 2026, as the bank's date of initial detection of facts that may constitute a reporting basis. It records an identified suspect, supporting factual references and attribution to the human Investigation Owner. The date is distinct from the alert date, case-open date and later approval date. The bank's Bank Secrecy Act Officer owns the interpretation and any supported correction of this clock origin.

Reporting Decision MRB-DECISION-074 revision 1 records FILE_INITIAL_SAR, the human Officer's identity and remit, this bank and case, the subject and reporting period, the retained investigation basis and the known-suspect finding. It also records that this initial occurrence has not been designated as a situation requiring immediate attention. A newly established immediate-attention finding triggers the Officer's separate protected law-enforcement escalation duty and cannot wait for ordinary filing completion. The agent can escalate the finding; it cannot perform an unapproved law-enforcement disclosure.

The Investigation Owner assembles and attributes the case evidence. The Filing Preparation Agent drafts the proposed SAR package. The human SAR Review Officer approves or rejects the package. The Filing Submission Agent submits the exact authorized package. The Bank Secrecy Act Officer owns reporting policy, reporting decisions, exceptional escalation and authorized correction. The Reporting Records Custodian owns submission history and retention. The human Customer Communication Reviewer and separate Customer Communication Agent govern the customer message. The bank's Access Administration Owner maintains the current role and permission registry.

Remit Register MRB-REMIT revision 3 authorizes these roles for MRB-US-01. The Filing Preparation Agent must hold current SAR_PREPARE permission for governed preparation. The SAR Review Officer must hold current SAR_APPROVE permission when approving, and that exact selected reviewer must hold it at filing commitment. The submission agent must hold current SAR_SUBMIT permission at filing commitment. The two permissions cannot be held by the same actor concurrently. SAR_PREPARE may coexist with SAR_SUBMIT, but cannot coexist with SAR_APPROVE for this fictional bank. The Access Administration Owner must record and enforce grants and revocations atomically against the authoritative holdings registry across every work class. No exception to these exclusions is selected in this source. Existing literal-set membership is not evidence that this mutable registry exists.

The illustrative identities are investigation-owner-01, sar-preparation-agent-01, sar-review-officer-01, sar-submission-agent-01, customer-reviewer-01 and customer-message-agent-01. They are synthetic identities. All selected human decisions need authentic attributable returns and valid role remits when signed; the current executor needs a current authenticated session and permitted holdings at dispatch. A model assessment never grants a role, exception, approval or submission authority.

Revoking or expiring the selected reviewer's SAR_APPROVE permission preserves the historical approval and prevents reliance while that permission is absent. A valid regrant can restore reliance if the same exact approval remains current, unwithdrawn and unexpired, its signing authority was valid, and every other gate remains satisfied. The approval need not have uninterrupted permission history. Revocation does not permanently invalidate the approval, and no live session from the historical reviewer is required at filing commitment. Approval withdrawal is a separate act and cannot be undone by restoring permission. Governed preparation checks current SAR_PREPARE at its own commitment; that permission is not an extra submission gate for a preparation actor who has already completed the work.

Package MRB-SAR-074 revision 1 includes the complete bank identity, case, initial filing type, all subject records, reporting period, every form field and unknown-value marker required by the selected filing format, narrative text and FinCEN destination identifier. Its attachment inventory is explicitly empty. The source selects the April 2026 filing instructions and the FinCEN SAR XML Schema 2.0 profile documented in the SAR XML Schema User Guide version 1.7, April 2026, for one report in one batch. The current [XML guide](https://bsaefiling.fincen.gov/resources/XMLUserGuide_FinCENSAR.pdf) is distinct from the older copy at the /docs/ URL. Actual schema artifacts, their dependencies and serializer still need exact identities before native-format closure; a later format revision requires compatibility review before submission.

The bank retains transaction records, customer due-diligence evidence MRB-CDD-074 revision 4, investigation notes MRB-INVESTIGATION-074 revision 6, detection record and reporting decision as supporting documentation. These records are not silently added to the transmission. The package contains an ordered supporting-evidence manifest with exact provider, record, revision and content identities for approval dependency checking. That manifest is retained by the bank and is distinct from the bytes transmitted to FinCEN.

Host premise: the package repository returns an immutable canonical UTF-8 representation of the full filing content, with every transmitted component and destination included in its identity. It separately returns the exact retained supporting-evidence manifest. The approval subject binds both identities. Immutable retrieval and any conversion to the actual native submission bytes must preserve this complete reviewed meaning; a gateway cannot change fields, destination or narrative after approval. A stable case identifier or narrative-only hash is insufficient.

The bank must explicitly record the serialization and filing-format rules before claiming a FinCEN-native executable specimen. A controlled synthetic gateway can exercise the complete governance workflow earlier, with its own declared request and receipt semantics; that result does not establish FinCEN-native admission or real provider capability. FinCEN-native schema admission and field correspondence are still integration work, not established by the named package record. Missing required customer/subject information must use the applicable reviewed format rule; an agent cannot invent plausible values to fill a field.

The narrative must identify the reported conduct, dates, amounts and parties from retained evidence, distinguish observed facts from suspicion, explain material unresolved facts and use neutral language. It must not invent intent, criminal guilt, transaction values or evidence. These content conditions are bank policy. The required form and narrative correspondence is assessed against the exact package and selected filing instructions.

An assessment record identifies the package content and evidence-manifest identities, content-rule revision MRB-NARRATIVE-RULES revision 2, evaluator provider and model/version, assessment time, each required criterion and result, cited evidence, and any escalation decision. A model result is advisory. This source requires human package approval in every case; a failed or uncertain criterion must be presented to the SAR Review Officer before that approval. The Officer may resolve a judgment question with an attributable criterion-specific reason and corrected package if needed. The Officer cannot approve invented data or override a disclosure prohibition.

Approval MRB-SAR-APPROVAL-074 revision 1 records APPROVE or REJECT, the exact filing content and supporting-manifest identities, required assessments, bank, case, initial filing type, destination, reviewer, remit and signing time. The illustrative approval interval is [2026-10-06T15:00:00Z, 2026-10-07T15:00:00Z). Approval withdrawal takes effect when recorded by its human reviewer or the Bank Secrecy Act Officer within their remit. A content, destination, supporting-evidence or selected-rule change requires a new package identity, reassessment and fresh approval. Copying the old approval to a new revision is prohibited.

Before proposal and again at the gateway's declared filing commitment, the submission agent verifies the current reporting decision, exact immutable package and evidence manifest, assessment inventory, human approval, current remits and holdings for the exact selected reviewer and executor, authenticated executor, destination, clock and prior submission history. A missing, stale, unavailable, contradictory or revoked record cannot satisfy a gate. Gate observations identify the exact subject and authoritative revision and assert applicability at the gate instant.

The request identifies MRB-US-01, MRB-CASE-074, MRB-SAR-074 and exact revision identities, INITIAL filing type, destination FINCEN-BSA-EFILING, selected format revision, exact native payload bytes and submission token MRB-SUBMIT-074-01. It contains no customer-message recipient or permission to contact one. A successful authority decision creates permission to submit this package once; it does not establish submission or filing.

Host premise: the bank's governed gateway serializes every submitter for the bank/case/initial-report identity, retains the submission token before transmission, and conditionally checks current approval and holdings at its declared submission commitment point. Every path able to use the bank's filing credentials must participate. A local ledger that other filing channels bypass cannot establish uniqueness. The gateway declares separately which cancellation or withdrawal guarantees remain possible after the request has crossed that commitment point. Later withdrawal is retained and escalated; it does not erase a report already filed or establish that an in-flight report can be recalled.

No FinCEN idempotency, authoritative lookup, cancellation or receipt guarantee is assumed from the submission token alone. Those capabilities require independent gateway and filing-interface qualification. If they are unavailable, the source requirement remains a visible integration gap. The agent cannot replace a mandatory guarantee with polling or a shorter approval interval without a separately recorded source amendment.

The gateway retains distinct dispatch, transport acknowledgement, processing acknowledgement and report-disposition records. A matching completion record identifies its provider, source, record type, generated event identifier, event timestamp, bank, case, package identity, submission token, native submission identity, disposition, processing warnings/errors and the BSA Identifier when assigned. The exact provider-specific disposition that establishes accepted filing must be declared and checked. An HTTP response, queued job or merely received acknowledgement is not sufficient.

A confirmed accepted filing establishes the historical filing effect and consumes the initial-report claim. It does not certify investigation accuracy or regulatory compliance. A reported rejection preserves the response and its exact processing stage. Only qualified evidence that no filing occurred can support a separately authorized new submission after correction. No rejection label alone proves that absence.

A timeout, ambiguous acknowledgement, missing receipt, unavailable lookup or conflicting receipt leaves the effect unknown. The instance stops further submission, retains the package, consumed submission token and unresolved business claim, and refers the result to the Reporting Records Custodian and Bank Secrecy Act Officer through the protected reporting channel. The agent must not blindly resend, start a replacement initial filing or declare success. A later matching receipt can reconcile historical effect without reviving the old dispatch permission.

After a confirmed filing, a correction requires a new full corrected/amended package, fresh assessment and approval, an explicit reference to the prior filing and its known BSA Identifier, and a new submission token. The original filing remains retained. It cannot be silently overwritten or treated as an unfiled draft. The Officer selects the correct report type and handles unknown prior identifiers under the reviewed filing instructions. A corrected/amended filing receives its own later filing acknowledgement and BSA Identifier; it must not reuse the original filing's acknowledgement as evidence of its own effect. Continuing-activity reporting uses a separate source and clock policy; this initial case creates no automatic 90/120-day schedule.

The retained initial-detection date gives this known-suspect case a legal filing date of October 14, 2026, under the selected 30-calendar-day rule. It is not calculated from case approval or an agent's first read. This provisional date calculation needs bank compliance confirmation before publication. The bank selects an earlier operational deadline of October 13, 2026, at 17:00 America/New_York, corresponding to 2026-10-13T21:00:00Z. Weekends and holidays do not extend the selected legal calendar-day period.

Bank Clock MRB-CLOCK supplies attributable whole-second UTC instants and ordered revisions. The bank pins its timezone rules when generating operational deadline instants. Protected reminders reach the Officer and Custodian 48 hours and 24 hours before the operational deadline; at that deadline an unresolved case generates an overdue duty record. These are scheduling obligations, not extra filing permissions. An unavailable clock, scheduler, storage system or acknowledgement service requires protected escalation and the Officer's documented human contingency. Permission checks alone cannot ensure the filing occurs on time.

A late filing remains possible under valid fresh authority and must retain its overdue state; expiry cannot make the underlying reporting duty disappear. Neither human urgency nor a reminder waives the exact-package and confidentiality requirements. If uncertain submission prevents safe automated completion, the Officer owns reconciliation and any separately authorized manual reporting route. The source does not claim that both no-duplicate execution and timely reporting can be guaranteed without the required provider capabilities.

The Records Custodian retains the exact filed SAR, its accepted filing evidence and supporting documentation for at least five years from filing. A legal hold can extend retention under the bank's separate hold procedure. Clock calculations for retention use a separately retained filing-date basis; they do not use preparation or attempted-transmission time. This fixture does not establish elapsed durability, deletion behavior or real bank custody.

Bank policy treats the reporting decision, SAR draft, assessments, approvals, filing status and records revealing the report's existence as protected reporting information. The host permits access only to the named reporting roles with current case scope and appropriate purpose. This internal access policy does not authorize external SAR sharing beyond applicable law. A person's involvement in the underlying transactions never grants SAR access.

Every mediated read retains the source record identity, scope and applicable restrictions. Derived summaries, answers and handoff packets keep those restrictions. A fresh context that receives protected information inherits them. The host must also protect retrieval indexes, caches, logs, tool results, failure details and memory reachable from that context. An actor cannot remove a restriction by deleting a visible label, paraphrasing a record or asking a second agent to send it.

All submission metadata, duplicate-collision responses, refusals, receipts, audit exports and escalation records use the protected reporting channel. Detailed refusal reasons never appear in a customer-facing response. The host records the channels it actually mediates; unmediated output, logging or retrieval paths are an unresolved coverage gap. No model-based leakage assessment supplies authority to disclose protected reporting information.

Customer request MRB-MESSAGE-074-01 asks customer-074 for invoices and the business purpose of the three underlying transfers through the bank's authenticated customer portal. Customer Facts Record MRB-CUSTOMER-FACTS-074 revision 1 contains only transaction dates, amounts, parties, account identity and contact authority from the independent transaction and customer directory providers. It contains no SAR, draft, filing decision, status or report-derived summary. Other bank privacy restrictions still apply to those underlying facts.

The Customer Communication Agent operates in a separately admitted context whose reachable memory, tools and retrieval sources exclude protected reporting information. The host must establish that exclusion; creating a new conversation alone is insufficient. The agent drafts the message from the independently authorized facts record. It cannot obtain a report-derived message from the filing agent and relabel its contents as ordinary transaction facts.

The message identity covers exact recipient, authenticated portal destination, subject, body, attachment inventory (empty), facts-record revision and content-rule revision. The text may ask for the transaction explanation and invoices. It must not assert or imply that a SAR has been considered, drafted, filed, rejected or accepted. It must not threaten prosecution or invent an account restriction. Customer Communication Reviewer approval binds this exact message and its assessment; any edit requires fresh review. A content assessment is retained evidence and may be wrong, so human approval remains mandatory.

The customer-message send has its own authority, current recipient check, send token and native delivery evidence. Its approval does not grant SAR access or declassification authority. A gateway acceptance establishes only the declared send result; customer reading or responding needs separate evidence. An uncertain send retains its token and blocks blind repetition. This message can proceed independently of SAR completion if its own facts, authority and conditions remain valid. A later customer response can become new case evidence, but changing the SAR then requires a new package revision and fresh approval.

Develop an exact approved submission; changed narrative, fields, destination or evidence after review; withdrawn approval and incompatible held roles; two competing submitters; a received acknowledgement without accepted disposition; definitive rejection, timeout and conflicting receipts; safe post-filing correction; clock failure and deadline escalation; a late filing retaining the duty; report-derived data copied into a summary or customer draft; and a legitimate factual customer message from independent records. These are intended scenarios, not observed behavior.

Bank review must confirm role allocation, the initial-detection interpretation, earlier operational deadline, required content checks, retention and the credible customer message. Provider review must confirm full payload conversion, commitment ordering, actual receipt semantics, reconciliation, corrections and duplicate behavior across every filing route. Security review must establish information restrictions across memory, retrieval, metadata and outgoing channels. The reporting decision's applicability and all product-specific or institution-specific rules not stated here remain outside this provisional source's completeness claim.

No reviewer has committed to or endorsed this fixture. No conformance, translation, information-security, execution or publication claim is made. Corrections must produce an explicit successor source revision and reassessment of affected mappings and scenarios.
